response.rationale: Lumbosacral radiculopathy best accounts for the L5–S1 disc herniation, positive straight-leg raise, progressive foot drop, and bilateral Achilles areflexia; peroneal neuropathy cannot explain flexor hallucis longus weakness or absent Achilles reflexes, and peripheral artery disease is excluded by normal arteriography.

rejected.why: Isolated peroneal neuropathy would spare flexor hallucis longus and the Achilles reflex, both of which are affected.
Decreased ankle-brachial indices are contradicted by lower-extremity arteriography showing no significant vascular lesions.
